briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Turns Bipartisan in Michigan While DEA and Psychedelics Momentum Builds Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis operators are getting real political cover for once — both major governor's race candidates are now campaigning on rolling back the 24% wholesale tax, and the state Supreme Court just narrowed police search powers in the industry's favor. Nationally, the DEA rescheduling case is moving toward a judge's recommendation while Compass Pathways just landed a fast-track FDA voucher for its psilocybin depression drug — real signals that federal cannabis and psychedelics policy is bending toward operators.

local.text: Lume Cannabis Co. opened its new Ann Arbor location at 2247 W. Liberty Street with a three-day grand-opening celebration, adding fresh retail footprint in one of the state's tightest college-town markets.

The Michigan Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that the smell of marijuana alone can't justify a warrantless vehicle search, and separately that even suspected civil-infraction possession doesn't meet the bar — a real win for consumers and operators tired of the lingering stigma.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a "Freedom Agenda" plank pledging to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax, arguing it "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections" — a sign tax relief is becoming a genuine bipartisan issue heading into November.

Democratic candidate and Genesee County Sheriff Chris Swanson has also vowed to roll back the tax, and the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association is now actively building momentum behind whichever candidate delivers relief — giving operators two viable paths to a fix.

The hard reality behind the political push: Higher Love Cannabis Co. suspended operations at five of its nine dispensaries this month citing the wholesale tax's "mounting tax burden," while State Rep. James DeSana's one-line repeal bill, HB 6224, gives the legislature a clean off-ramp if lawmakers act.

national.text: DEA released the full 2,533-page transcript of its cannabis rescheduling hearing as Chief Administrative Law Judge Derek Julius prepares his recommendation, with the agency's own brief arguing marijuana "no longer fits the statutory requirements for Schedule I."

The FDA granted Compass Pathways a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for its synthetic psilocybin drug COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, a designation that could shorten review to just one to two months after filing.

SNDL closed its acquisition of Surterra Holdings via a Sunstream Bancorp foreclosure, picking up indirect majority exposure to 43 Surterra Wellness dispensaries and a 175,000-square-foot Florida production facility as part of a 56-store, roughly $150 million-revenue platform spanning Florida, Texas and Massachusetts.

Vireo Growth and Planet 13 announced a definitive merger that would make Vireo the second-largest dispensary network in Florida with roughly 106 dispensaries and 329,000 square feet of cultivation and production capacity, pending regulatory sign-off.

Grown Rogue International closed initial transactions to enter the New York market through a planned acquisition of PharmaCann's license and assets, forming a joint venture with a capital partner contributing up to $15 million and picking up four Verilife-branded dispensaries plus a 24,000-square-foot cultivation facility.
